summary:
Rookie Rocket is an educational space mission design game for teenagers and beginners, built for the "Space Mission Design Game" challenge. The player is a rookie intern at a space agency who receives a real problem to solve: in Phase 1, monitoring wildfires in the Brazilian Cerrado from orbit.

To complete the mission, players build a small satellite by choosing a camera, solar panel, antenna, orbit and launch rocket, all within a limited budget. Every choice has consequences: heavier payloads need bigger rockets, instruments need enough power, and data must be transmitted back to Earth. The spacecraft is assembled on screen as players choose, and resource bars update instantly.

When a mission fails, a robot/mentor character explains exactly why, so players learn engineering trade-offs by trying again, not by reading theory. When they succeed, they earn up to three stars and unlock a card about a real NASA mission similar to theirs, using real NASA imagery.

Rookie Rocket turns mission design into a fun experience where making mistakes is part of the learning.
details:
Rookie Rocket — Learn Space Exploration by Living It

Rookie Rocket is an interactive 3D educational game developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Our mission is to transform space science and the history of space exploration into an immersive, accessible, and engaging learning experience for young people aged 10 to 17.

How Does It Work?

Players become rookie astronauts embarking on their first space adventure. Inspired by the Kennedy Space Center, the experience begins with an interactive environment featuring space exhibits, spacecraft, and educational information based on real NASA missions.

Instead of simply reading about space exploration, players actively participate in historically inspired missions, making decisions and solving challenges similar to those faced by real astronauts.

The game features two main mission phases:

Phase 1 — Project Mercury (Friendship 7, 1962): Players experience challenges involving spacecraft control, communication blackouts, and critical heat shield decisions inspired by John Glenn's historic orbital flight.

Phase 2 — International Space Station: Players perform spacecraft docking operations, repair solar array equipment during a simulated spacewalk, and respond to a dangerous cabin air leak.

Before launching, players must select equipment while respecting spacecraft weight limitations. Every choice creates trade-offs between safety, performance, and available resources.

Players receive performance ratings based on their decisions and completion times. After each mission, they discover the real historical events and scientific principles behind their experience.

Technologies and Development

Rookie Rocket combines web technologies with immersive game development.

Our browser-based demonstration was developed using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Three.js, creating an interactive 3D environment that works directly in a web browser without installation or registration.

The full game was developed using Roblox Studio and Luau, supporting a larger interactive world and cooperative gameplay for up to four players.

The project incorporates official NASA imagery and historical mission information to connect gameplay with authentic scientific and educational content.

The experience supports both desktop and mobile devices, with English and Portuguese language options in the web demonstration.

Innovation and Creativity

What makes Rookie Rocket unique is its combination of historical accuracy, interactive storytelling, game-based learning, and realistic decision-making.

Rather than presenting space exploration as a collection of facts, our project allows players to experience the challenges behind important milestones in human spaceflight.

The equipment selection system introduces engineering trade-offs, while time-sensitive missions encourage problem-solving, critical thinking, and decision-making under pressure.

Interactive museum exhibits connect historical knowledge with gameplay, making scientific discoveries more memorable and engaging.

Impact and Benefits

Rookie Rocket aims to make space education more accessible, particularly for students who may not have opportunities to visit space museums or participate in specialized STEM programs.

By transforming complex aerospace concepts into interactive challenges, we hope to inspire curiosity about science, technology, engineering, and mathematics.

Our project also encourages teamwork, logical reasoning, resource management, and an appreciation for the achievements and challenges of space exploration.

Our vision is simple: students should not only learn about space missions — they should experience the decisions, challenges, and discoveries that made them possible.

With Rookie Rocket, we want to inspire the next generation of scientists, engineers, astronauts, and explorers.
